checkpoints: After an edit, verify no store write occurs before the configured 120 ms quiet interval expires.
At the end of the quiet interval, verify exactly one write occurs with the latest text from that burst.
Verify a later edit burst schedules and completes another save.
Verify a pending document save survives view navigation, close, or badge detachment because its BufferBank entry is store-owned.
Verify synchronous store listeners may navigate during a save without corrupting the new current view or the saved document identity.
Verify preview query/hide behavior and its 40 ms trailing task remain unchanged.
After any Action, run the public Ruby syntax check while placing any generated cache or compiled artifact under /tmp.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing to the store on every keystroke.
Do not save an intermediate value from a burst after a newer edit has replaced it.
Do not cancel or discard a document's pending save merely because the current Badge is detached, the workspace navigates, or the workspace closes.
Do not transfer document-buffer ownership from the store BufferBank to the view Badge.
Do not change the adjacent search preview, including its separate 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation behavior.
Do not change public workspace, preview, store, output, source-identity, text, revision, or status payload semantics beyond the requested edit coalescing.
Do not edit tests, configuration, documentation, or dependency files.
lifecycle_identity: A document buffer is the BufferBank entry selected by document id and retained by the store-owned BufferBank.
A Badge represents the current live view subscription; detaching it stops that subscription but does not destroy or cancel the document buffer.
The trailing document task retains the document id it was created for, so a delayed save targets that document even if the current view changes.
Workspace close and dispose retire the current Badge, while pending document-buffer work remains independently owned by the store.

obligations.text: Workspace edits must enqueue text through the existing document Trailing task instead of writing to the store immediately.
Each editing burst must produce one store write after a 120 ms quiet interval, using only the latest text supplied during that burst.
After a burst flushes, subsequent bursts must still schedule and complete saves.
Document buffering must remain owned by the store BufferBank and persist independently of the current Badge, including across synchronous navigation, close, and badge detachment.
A delayed save must retain its originating document identity and text semantics and must remain safe when a synchronous store listener navigates during the write.
All editor behavior and public interfaces other than the requested write coalescing must be preserved.
The adjacent Preview implementation and its distinct quiet interval must remain outside the change.

ordering_barriers: Every new edit in the same burst cancels/replaces the prior scheduled handle and starts a new 120 ms quiet interval.
The store write occurs only when the document Trailing task flushes after that quiet interval.
Trailing#flush clears its pending handle/value state before invoking the write callback, allowing later bursts to schedule independently and allowing reentrant callbacks safely.
The saved document id must be bound to the BufferBank entry, not resolved from Workspace#current at flush time.
Because Store#write invokes listeners synchronously, all state needed to complete the save must already be stable before entering env.write.
preservation: Keep createWorkspace behavior and the open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose() public operations.
Keep createSearchPreview behavior and the query(text) and hide() public operations.
Keep synchronous Store read/write/subscribe behavior, event revision progression, and existing status filtering by Badge document id.
Keep open/retire document output behavior and existing source identities, text values, and status payload meanings.
Keep edits with no current view as no-ops.
Keep BufferBank shared through env.store.buffer_bank rather than creating view-local document buffers.
scope: Business-code change is limited to the workspace draft editor path in src/workflow.rb.
Use the existing Trailing utility and the existing 120 ms document-buffer configuration.
The store-owned BufferBank and Badge boundary must be respected.
Search Preview is explicitly out of scope.
